guyana.title: Flag of the Co-operative Republic of Guyana

colors.note: Background field; represents the forests and agricultural richness of Guyana.
Large triangle pointing from the hoist; represents mineral wealth.
Small triangle overlaid on the gold; symbolises the zeal and dynamism of nation-building.
Narrow border around the gold triangle; represents the many rivers and waters of Guyana.
Narrow border around the red triangle; stands for the endurance of the Guyanese people.

desc:
- A green field with a large gold isosceles triangle pointing from the hoist, overlaid with a smaller red triangle, with white and black fimbriations
- Known as the Golden Arrowhead, designed by American vexillologist Whitney Smith in the early 1960s
- Adopted on 26 May 1966 upon independence from the United Kingdom
trivia:
- Nicknamed the Golden Arrowhead, a reference to the forward-pointing triangles symbolising progress
- Whitney Smith, who designed the flag, later founded the Flag Research Center and coined the term vexillology
- The flag's five colours each carry distinct meaning, an unusually rich symbolic scheme among modern national flags
